findings.problem: 'They found them, because the questions supplied the answers' is a blanket causal claim. The papal church's link to this movement now cites Wattenbach on the 1367 Erfurt case: the answers went far beyond the questions and the man seemed truly convinced. Lerner's thesis, as the movement itself states it, is that no organized sect existed, not that every answer was supplied. The sentence must be narrowed so the movement and its own link agree.
findings.evidence: wattenbach_...1887.txt:5719-5723: 'Aber hier gehen die Antworten weit hinaus über die Fragepunkte, und enthalten eine Fülle ganz individueller Züge. Der Inquisit scheint ... von der Wahrheit seines Wahnes wirklich überzeugt zu sein'; his caution at 5717-5719 is about the questions following the Clementine schema.
findings.proposed_fix: why: replace 'They found them, because the questions supplied the answers.' with 'They found them, often because the questions supplied the answers.' (field FRE 61.8, FK 8.9). longDescription: replace 'and found them, because the questions supplied the answers.' with 'and found them, often because the questions supplied the answers.' findings.problem: Settled, not passed on: 'a brewer's wife' is wrong. Margery's own Book says she herself took up brewing (for three or four years) and failed. Her husband John Kempe was a burgess of Lynn, not a brewer. The Book also names her as the daughter of John Brunham, five times mayor of Lynn. The Book (Windeatt) is on the movement's own source list but is not vendored. The correction rests on the Book, ch. 2 and the Proem/ch. 1, which every edition prints.
findings.evidence: The Book of Margery Kempe I.2 ('she began to brew, and was one of the greatest brewers in the town of N. for three or four years'); I.1 and later chapters on her father John of Burnham, mayor of Lynn. Not vendored; add to wants.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace 'Margery Kempe was a brewer's wife from Bishop's Lynn who could not write.' with 'Margery Kempe, a mayor's daughter from Bishop's Lynn, ran a brewery of her own for a few years. She could not write.' (field FRE 66.8, FK 7.1). Add to wants: a public-domain text of The Book of Margery Kempe.

findings.problem: The rewrite moves the field's own judgment into Alfred's mouth: 'The Viking wars nearly killed English Christianity, by Alfred of Wessex's account.' Alfred's preface to the Pastoral Care says that learning had fallen away and that the churches had been ravaged and burned. It does not say Christianity nearly died. The 'reported' form must name what the witness reports, not more.
findings.evidence: Alfred, preface to the Pastoral Care (not vendored; wanted per the draft): 'Swæ clæne hio wæs oðfeallenu on Angelcynne ...' (learning had so utterly decayed) and 'ær ðæm ðe hit eall forhergod wære ond forbærned' (before it was all ravaged and burned).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace 'The Viking wars nearly killed English Christianity, by Alfred of Wessex's account. He wrote that the churches had been ravaged and burned.' with 'In the Viking wars, Alfred of Wessex wrote, the churches were ravaged and burned, and learning all but died out.' (with R1-08's change too, field FRE 63.5, FK 8.1).

findings.problem: The fact is marked sourced, but the rewrite says more than the source shows. Evans (quoting Gibbon) shows Byzantine persecution, people condemned to the flames, and the Tephrike state and its fall. It does not show armies, or people driven from their homes (his 'transplantation' is Constantine V's resettlement in Thrace, another event). Separately, in why, 'they raided the empire's lands until it fell in 878' now makes 'it' read as the empire.
findings.evidence: evans_through-bosnia-and-the-herzegovina-on-foot_1877.txt:1092-1097: 'when the persecution of Byzantium had provoked the Paulicians ... when the Roman Emperor fled before the heretics whom his mother had condemned to the flames, and Tephrice became the capital of a free-state'; 1086-1090 transplantation under Constantine V; 1107 'The fall of the Paulician free-state of Tephrice'.
findings.proposed_fix: why: replace 'Imperial armies killed them and drove them from their homes.' with 'The empire persecuted them, and many were burned.' and 'until it fell in 878.' with 'until the town fell in 878.' (field FRE 60.9, FK 7.6). longDescription: replace 'Imperial armies killed and uprooted them in large numbers.' with 'The empire persecuted them, and many were burned.' (field FRE 62.4, FK 8.2).

notes: Validator: node tools/validate-census.mjs --base <origin/main census> gives 0 errors and 2 shortName warnings that were there before. The census matches the three drafts exactly: 26 movement fields, 10 changed edges, 3 new edges, 1 retired link. Every quote on the 11 drafted links (42) and on the 12 ruling 6 fact sources matches its file at the stated lines. Context reads: Mouravieff 1720-1730, 1920-1930, 2290-2298; Langlois 5094-5106, 5210-5220; Ormanian 1660-1700, 1740-1760, 1795-1805; HP 7130-7190; Glassberger 37420-37520 and preface 528-545; NPNF Reg. I.77 33795-33815; Teresa 21984-22018; Bullarium 85925-85960, 86170-86192; Lea III index 37338-37380; Evans 1084-1110; Fermendzin 1326-1340; Brezova 54870-54900; Griffith 4425-4450; Alcuin 64368-64376. Ruling 2: Kyiv and the Carmelites are rightly re-typed; both are authority acts (consecration by the patriarch; papal approval of a corrected rule at the order's request). The Numidia-Gregory outcome is sound under (c): Reg. I.77 keeps the Numidian custom for primates and bars bishops who had come from the Donatists. Ite vos is adequately sourced. The chronicle names the bull of union and gives its content ('unum corpus ... unimus', 37513-37515), along with the bull of concord. The editors' preface (536-539) gives the result: two separate orders in 1517. The OCR '1317' is answered by the editors' footnote and preface. Persia-St Thomas left as influenced: the reason given is half right. Movement dates that do not overlap do rule out in contact with, because the 550 act falls before the 849 movement. That fact does not make influence true. The link stands only because it is Inferential-Thin and its note says plainly that no source ties Cosmas to the Kerala church. Keeping it is defensible; retiring it is a fair P2-L11 question. No finding. Ruling 5: the retirement entry is well formed, and its replacedBy link exists and carries the 1367 case. The Free Spirit link's rewrite is sound; 'judged sincere' is a fair, slightly firm reading of Wattenbach's 'scheint ... wirklich überzeugt'. Two-way check passes: the era 6 movement keeps one link (Taborites), which its text names. The Free Spirit sentence is a comparison, not a claimed tie. Ruling 6: the classification of all 53 facts is accepted (35 plain, 18 guarded). Breslau: the Lea vol. III index line ('Jews ... burned by Capistrano in Breslau, ii. 549') is Lea's own statement, read at vendored lines. With the 1447 letter (Capistrano made enforcer of the decrees on Jews and Muslims 'in omnibus Italiae partibus') it is enough to count as sourced, though thin: vol. II p. 549 should stay wanted. The rewritten Breslau sentences claim no more than the two sources show. John Paul II 2001: settled as stands. In Athens on 4 May 2001 he said the sack 'fills Catholics with deep regret' and begged forgiveness for Catholic sins against the Orthodox. It was widely reported as an apology; 'voiced deep regret' would be more exact but is not required. Kesrwan: Duwayhi dates the march 1307, and the text says 'around 1305'. That is a date, not a guarded fact, and it is left. Outside this review's findings: cft-website/index.html embeds an older census copy (292 entries) that still shows 'the Hakkari Remnant', the old schism text and the retired link. This is the known embedded-data exception (tools/embedded-world-data-baseline.txt) and needs its re-sync. Public text in all changed fields is in American spelling and has no build narration, apart from R1-12. Every changed field passes Reading Ease >= 60 and FK <= 10, apart from R1-12. One new sentence runs past 25 words (R1-10).
